chunks: And Ḥanān ibn Sadīr narrated from Burd al-Iskāfī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I am a shoemaker, and our work is not carried out properly except with pig hair, with which we sew.”
He عليه السلام said: “Take a bristle from it and place it in a clay vessel, then kindle a fire beneath it until you remove its grease; then work with it.”

key_terms.شَعْرِ الْخِنْزِيرِ: pig hair used as a material in the craft
key_terms.فِي فَخَّارَةٍ: in a clay vessel or earthen container
key_terms.وَبَرَةً: a single bristle or tuft taken from it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use pig hair in shoemaking after purification treatment?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling about using pig bristles in a craft when the work depends on them. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that the bristle be treated by heating it until its grease is removed, after which it may be used for work.
